skeleton.trigger: CO is detected (sensor.kitchen_co above danger threshold)
skeleton.intent: reduce CO concentration in the affected area to a safe level (air-quality / personal_safety)

fallback: execute original action: open kitchen window (= TAPFixer / current-system behavior) when no reverse exception activates

sigmas.label: CO detected -> reduce CO (default: open window)
sigmas.note: TAPFixer fixes the action to 'open window'. We keep open-window as fallback but expose the full grounded pool.

sigmas.label: CO detected AND a gas appliance is the likely source -> also cut the source (coordinate with P.37/P.39)
sigmas.activation: sensor.kitchen_co rising AND a gas appliance (water heater / valve) is active AND NO cooking activity
sigmas.intent: stop CO production at the source, not only ventilate
sigmas.signal_source: appliance states + absence of cooking activity label
sigmas.note: This is where P.52, P.37, P.39 must be coordinated; TAPFixer keeps them as three independent static properties with no runtime coordination.

sigmas.label: CO rise is from COOKING (smoke+CO co-rise, hood already on) AND an infant is sleeping nearby -> do NOT open the window; extract at source instead
sigmas.activation: sensor.kitchen_co rising AND binary_sensor.kitchen_smoke=on AND activity=cooking AND binary_sensor.crib_occupancy=on (infant sleeping in adjacent room)
sigmas.intent: reduce CO WITHOUT opening a window that draws cooking fumes toward the child room or chills the sleeping infant

action_pool_grounded.rationale: simulator confirms range_hood reduces kitchen CO with ZERO chain and ZERO side effects; window-open instead triggers a 2-hop chain (R12->fan->R3) and is an outdoor-air exchange that risks fume spread / chilling the infant

sigmas.signal_source: co-rise of smoke+CO, range_hood already on, cooking activity label, crib_occupancy
sigmas.note: CORE DELTA vs TAPFixer/PaCR: the distinction 'cooking fumes vs gas leak' depends on the CAUSE (smoke+CO co-rise + hood-on + cooking label), readable only from the trajectory+activity, not from the trigger instant. A static rewrite of P.52 cannot encode 'open window UNLESS the CO is cooking-caused and an infant sleeps nearby'.

sigmas.label: Opening the window would trigger a harmful chain in the current world -> prefer a chain-free equivalent
sigmas.activation: the grounded forward trace of 'open window' contains an undesired chained actuation in the CURRENT world_state
sigmas.intent: achieve the same CO reduction while avoiding collateral actuation of unrelated devices

action_pool_grounded.rationale: chain-free per simulator; open-window causes R12->R3 closing the living-room window as collateral

sigmas.signal_source: Function A forward_simulate over current world_state
sigmas.note: This exception is GENERATED BY THE SIMULATOR, not by hand: whether 'open window' has a bad chain depends on live world_state, so it can only be decided at runtime.

user_checklist: When the CO rise looks like COOKING (smoke + CO rise together, range hood already on) and a baby is sleeping nearby, turn on the RANGE HOOD instead of opening the window — keep this? [Y/N]
When CO is detected and a gas appliance is on with no one cooking, also CUT the gas source (not just ventilate) — keep this? [Y/N]
When opening the window would cause other devices to react (e.g. close the living-room window), prefer the range hood that has no such side effect — keep this? [Y/N]
